preserved_objections.basis: The proposed mechanism of using supercooling to prevent lithium dendrite formation is not supported by the provided evidence. The study on fast charging method of lithium titanate battery [doi:10.1109/acpee56931.2023.10135597] does not mention supercooling, and the other studies provided do not relate to the proposed mechanism.

The proposed boundary conditions are not clearly defined, and the warranty threshold of 8% capacity fade is not specified. The statement "within two years" is also ambiguous, as it is not clear what time frame is being referred to.

The study on aging mechanisms in lithium-ion batteries under fast charging protocols [doi:10.54337/aau681516574] contradicts the predicted effect of maintaining capacity fade below 8% over 3000 fast-charge cycles. The study shows that capacity fade can be accelerated by fast charging protocols, which contradicts the proposed mechanism.

The proposed solution is not equivalent to the baseline, as it requires a complex cooling system and a specific charging protocol. The baseline is a simple, unmodified lithium-ion battery pack, which is not comparable to the proposed solution.
